page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ine.large is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor within the Enhanced family. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per core to target compute-centric operations over memory-intensive demands.

Storage and networking specifications highlight a cloud-native architecture reliant on decoupled infrastructure. The server contains no onboard local disk storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data and boot operations. Zero discrete GPUs are bundled with this instance type. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

From an efficiency perspective, the provision of dedicated Intel CPU cores ensures deterministic execution without the variability found in shared or burstable environments. The configuration is functionally suited for compute-bound tasks with lean memory footprints, such as CI/CD build agents, decoupled batch computational workers, stateless API microservices, and lightweight web service endpoints.

It delivers 2 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs clocked at 2.7 GHz and 4.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring network-attached cloud storage for data persistence, and features no GPU acceleration. Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. Because processing resources are fully dedicated, it avoids CPU credit throttling and performance variance typical of burstable tiers. This hardware profile is appropriate for compute-oriented tasks with moderate memory requirements, including microservices, front-end web proxies, automated integration workers, and decoupled batch processing jobs.
